questions.q: Which table stores every user record in a ServiceNow instance?
options: sys_user
sys_user_group
sys_user_role
sys_user_has_role
questions.explain: sys_user is the single source of truth for every person who can log in, from agents to end users to integration accounts.

questions.q: A user's active field is set to false, but their locked_out field is also false. Can they log in?
options: Yes, as long as they know their password and username
No — active=false blocks login regardless of locked_out
Only if they have the admin role
Only during business hours
questions.explain: active is the master login gate. A false value blocks login completely, independent of locked_out or any role the user holds.

questions.q: What does the locked_out field represent, and how is it different from active?
options: It's just another name for the active field
It controls whether a user appears in reports
It's a separate gate, typically set after failed login attempts or a manual security action, independent of whether the user is otherwise active
It only applies to users with the admin role
questions.explain: locked_out and active answer different questions — one is about deliberate lockout (e.g. failed attempts), the other about whether the person is still a valid user at all.

questions.q: Why should you deactivate a departing employee's user record instead of deleting it?
options: Deactivation is faster to click than deletion
Deleting the record breaks or orphans every reference to that user across the instance, such as who reported an incident or approved a change
ServiceNow does not technically allow deleting sys_user records
Deactivated users still appear as active on reports, which admins prefer
questions.explain: sys_user is referenced from caller_id, opened_by, assigned_to, approvals, and audit history platform-wide; deleting it loses or breaks that historical trail.

questions.q: A brand-new user record is created and saved with active = true but zero roles assigned. What can they do?
options: Nothing at all, including logging in
Full administrative access by default
Very little beyond viewing their own profile and whatever default guest-level access exposes, until a role is assigned
They automatically inherit the itil role
questions.explain: A user record alone grants almost nothing meaningful; real functional access comes from role assignment, covered in Lesson 3.
